title: Linear Gaussian inverse posteriors and Tikhonov

items.title: Support and pseudoinverse coordinates of a finite singular Gaussian
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge1$, $m\in\mathbb R^n$, and let
$C\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric with $v^TCv\ge0$ for every
$v\in\mathbb R^n$. Let
$X$ be a random vector with law $N_n(m,C)$, and define
$\mu_X(E)=\mathbb P(X\in E)$ for Borel $E\subseteq\mathbb R^n$. Write
$\operatorname{Ran}(C)=\{Cv:v\in\mathbb R^n\}$, and put
$r=\dim\operatorname{Ran}(C)$. For a Borel probability $\mu$ on
$\mathbb R^n$, define its topological support by
$$ \operatorname{supp}(\mu)=\{x:\mu(B(x,\varepsilon))>0\text{ for every }\varepsilon>0\}, $$
where $B(x,\varepsilon)$ is the open Euclidean ball. If $r>0$, there are
$U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}$ and a symmetric positive-definite
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}$ with $U^TU=I_r$ such that
$$ C=U\Lambda U^T,\qquad \operatorname{Ran}(C)=\operatorname{Ran}(U),\qquad C^\dagger=U\Lambda^{-1}U^T. $$
Moreover, $X$ has the same law as $m+U\Lambda^{1/2}Z$, where
$Z\sim N_r(0,I_r)$, and
$$ \operatorname{supp}(\mu_X)=m+\operatorname{Ran}(C). $$
Here $C^\dagger$ is the unique matrix satisfying
$CC^\dagger C=C$, $C^\dagger CC^\dagger=C^\dagger$, and such that
$CC^\dagger$ and $C^\dagger C$ are symmetric. If $r=0$, then
$C=0$, $X=m$ almost surely, $C^\dagger=0$, and the support is $\{m\}$.

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, arXiv:2001.00617v2 (2021)
references.locator: Chapter 13, printed pp. 127–131 (PDF pp. 129–133), for the finite-dimensional Gaussian inverse-problem setting; the rank-deficient support and pseudoinverse-coordinate statement is proved locally.

references.title: M. Dashti and A. M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems (full lecture notes, arXiv:1302.6989)

items.title: Finite linear Gaussian inverse posterior with singular prior covariance
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $n,m\ge1$, $m_0\in\mathbb R^n$, and let
$C_0\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric with $v^TC_0v\ge0$ for every
$v\in\mathbb R^n$. Let
$A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ and let
$\Gamma\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$ be symmetric positive definite, meaning
$u^T\Gamma u>0$ for every nonzero $u\in\mathbb R^m$. Suppose
$X$ and $\eta$ are independent random vectors with laws
$X\sim N_n(m_0,C_0)$ and $\eta\sim N_m(0,\Gamma)$, and set
$Y=AX+\eta$. Define $\mu_0(E)=\mathbb P(X\in E)$ for Borel
$E\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, and set
$S=AC_0A^T+\Gamma$. Then $S$ is positive definite. For each
$y\in\mathbb R^m$, define
$$ \Phi_y(x)=\tfrac12(y-Ax)^T\Gamma^{-1}(y-Ax),\qquad Z(y)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{-\Phi_y(x)}\,\mu_0(dx). $$
For every $y$, $0<Z(y)<\infty$, so the normalized potential update
$$ \Pi^y(E)=\frac{\int_E e^{-\Phi_y(x)}\,\mu_0(dx)}{Z(y)} \quad(E\in\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n)) $$
is a probability measure and equals the conditional-law version obtained by
conditioning the observation model at $y$. Its Gaussian formula, defined for
every $y$, is
$$ N_n\!\left( m_0+C_0A^TS^{-1}(y-Am_0),\ C_0-C_0A^TS^{-1}AC_0 \right). $$
Let $P_Y(B)=\mathbb P(Y\in B)$ for Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^m$.
Conditional-law versions are unique only $P_Y$-almost surely. The displayed
mean and covariance formulas invert only $S$, not $C_0$; $C_0$ and the
posterior covariance may be singular. The prior support is
$m_0+\operatorname{Ran}(C_0)$.

items.title: Finite Gaussian MAP, posterior mean, and support-restricted Tikhonov minimizer coincide
items.statement:
Assume AC and let $n,m\ge1$, $m_0\in\mathbb R^n$,
$C_0\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ symmetric with $v^TC_0v\ge0$ for all
$v\in\mathbb R^n$,
$A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, and
$\Gamma\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$ symmetric with $u^T\Gamma u>0$ for all
nonzero $u\in\mathbb R^m$. Let
$X\sim N_n(m_0,C_0)$ and $\eta\sim N_m(0,\Gamma)$ be independent, and
observe $Y=AX+\eta$. Put
$S_0=m_0+\operatorname{Ran}(C_0)$ and
$r=\dim\operatorname{Ran}(C_0)$. The $r$-dimensional Euclidean Lebesgue
measure on $S_0$ is the pushforward of Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^r$
under any affine isometry onto $S_0$; this measure is independent of the
chosen orthonormal coordinates. A MAP point means a maximizer of the
posterior density with respect to this measure; for $r=0$, the unique point
of $S_0$ is the MAP point. The Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse $C_0^\dagger$
satisfies
$$ C_0C_0^\dagger C_0=C_0,\qquad C_0^\dagger C_0C_0^\dagger=C_0^\dagger, $$
and $C_0C_0^\dagger$ and $C_0^\dagger C_0$ are symmetric. The optimization
below is restricted to $S_0$. Then for every $y\in\mathbb R^m$, the unique
MAP point equals the posterior mean and the unique minimizer over $x\in S_0$ of
$$ J_y(x)=(Ax-y)^T\Gamma^{-1}(Ax-y) +(x-m_0)^TC_0^\dagger(x-m_0). $$
All objects are finite-dimensional; no minimization over points outside the
prior support is asserted when $C_0$ is singular.

title: Linear Gaussian inverse posteriors and Tikhonov — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A rank-one prior gives a singular Gaussian inverse posterior
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let
$X\sim N_2(0,\operatorname{diag}(1,0))$,
$\eta\sim N_2(0,I_2)$ independently, $A=I_2$, and observe
$y=(2,3)^T$ in the model $Y=AX+\eta$. The prior support is
$S_0=\{(t,0)^T:t\in\mathbb R\}$. The Gaussian posterior version has mean
$(1,0)^T$ and covariance $\operatorname{diag}(1/2,0)$. On $S_0$, the
support-restricted objective is
$$ J_y(x)=(x_1-2)^2+(x_2-3)^2+x_1^2, $$
and its unique minimizer is $(1,0)^T$.

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, arXiv:2001.00617v2 (2021)
references.locator: Chapter 13, printed pp. 127–131 (PDF pp. 129–133), finite-dimensional Gaussian MAP/Tikhonov context; the singular example is computed locally.

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the finite Gaussian posterior model. The example's matrix and one-variable quadratic calculations use no stronger choice principle.

items.title: Prior whitening turns an anisotropic Gaussian posterior into Tikhonov form
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X\sim N_2(0,\operatorname{diag}(4,1))$,
$\eta\sim N_2(0,\operatorname{diag}(1,4))$ independently, $A=I_2$, and
observe $y=(2,4)^T$ in $Y=AX+\eta$. Put
$L=\operatorname{diag}(2,1)$ and
$W=\operatorname{diag}(1,1/2)$. The coordinate change $x=Lz$ makes the
prior on $z$ standard Gaussian, and $W$ whitens the observation noise in
that $W\Gamma W^T=I_2$. The
preconditioned Tikhonov objective is
$$ \|WALz-Wy\|_2^2+\|z\|_2^2 =\|\operatorname{diag}(2,1/2)z-(2,2)^T\|_2^2+\|z\|_2^2. $$
The posterior mean, MAP point, and minimizer in the original parameter
coordinates are $(8/5,4/5)^T$, and the posterior covariance is
$(4/5)I_2$.

items.title: A non-Gaussian posterior can have different MAP and mean
items.statement:
For every probability density $p$ on $\mathbb R$ with finite first absolute
moment and at least one global maximizer, every maximum a posteriori (MAP)
point, meaning every global maximizer of $p$, equals its mean
$\int_{\mathbb R}t\,p(t)\,dt$.

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, arXiv:2001.00617v2 (2021)
references.locator: Chapter 13, printed pp. 127–131 (PDF pp. 129–133), discussion after equation (13.4): the conditional mean need not generally coincide with MAP when the prior or likelihood is non-Gaussian or the inverse problem is nonlinear; the bounded-support witness is proved locally.

references.title: M. Dashti and A. M. Stuart, The Bayesian Approach to Inverse Problems (full lecture notes, arXiv:1302.6989)
references.locator: §§3.1–3.2 for the posterior as a normalized likelihood update; the explicit non-Gaussian witness is proved locally.
